title: Carpet Cleaning Software: 8 Tools for Booking, Crews and Pay
html:
Carpet cleaning software has to book the job, send the crew and collect payment, and most owners need only one app for all three. Start with a job app such as Jobber or Kickserv, add Wave or QuickBooks for the books, and claim a free Google Business Profile. Published plans here run from $0 to $299 a month.

Carpet cleaning is a same-week business. A homeowner calls about a stain, wants a time window and expects a price before the van arrives. Software for this trade is judged on how fast it books that window and gets the invoice paid.

This guide sorts eight tools by the job each one does. Every price comes from the vendor page linked beside it, read in November 2026, and each tool gets one real limit.

Which carpet cleaning software books jobs and schedules crews?

Jobber, Housecall Pro and Kickserv all book and schedule carpet cleaning crews. They differ on price, seats and how much automation sits in the entry plan.

ToolEntry planPrice shownUsers
Jobber CoreCore$49 monthly, $29 billed annually1
Housecall Pro BasicBasic$79 monthly, $59 billed annually1
Housecall Pro EssentialsEssentials$189 monthly, $149 billed annually5
Kickserv StartStart$60 monthly5

Published list prices from each vendor page, November 2026. Taxes, add-ons and card fees are extra.

Price lists belong in the app from day one. Many carpet companies price per room, per square foot or by a minimum charge. Enter each rule once, with add-ons such as protector, deodorizer and stain treatment, so every quote uses the same numbers.

Time windows matter more than exact times. A homeowner will accept an arrival window of two hours. Look for online booking that shows only the windows you can actually serve, so the calendar never overbooks a van.

Photo notes help too. A before photo of a stain, taken at the door, protects you if the customer later says the spot was never there. Jobber lists unlimited photo and video storage only on Plus, and Housecall Pro lists photo reports on Essentials.

Carpet crews also need travel buffers. A truck-mount setup takes time to hook up and drain, and a three-room job is not a one-hour stop. Set job durations by room count in your first week so the schedule matches reality.

Which carpet cleaning business software suits a growing company?

Service Fusion and Workiz are built for companies with several vans and office staff. Both cost more than a one-user app, so they fit once you dispatch daily.

  • Service Fusion: customer management, estimates and jobs, scheduling and dispatching, integrated payments and invoicing with unlimited users. Starter is $208 a month billed annually, and plans are month to month. Limit: the page offers a demo instead of a free trial.
  • Workiz: scheduling, invoices, jobs and estimates on Standard, Pro and Ultimate, with unlimited jobs, estimates and clients on every plan. Automations are capped at 5, 10 and 30 across those plans. Limit: the page shows request pricing instead of a price.

Test the customer side as well as your own. Book a fake job from your phone and read the confirmation text. If the message is confusing, your customers will call you anyway, and the software has saved you nothing.

Dispatch tools earn their cost when two or more vans run at once. One person can juggle two vans from a phone. Three vans and a part-time scheduler need a shared board that shows where each van is and what is next.

Ask each vendor how a repeat customer is handled. Carpet cleaning is a rebooking business, and a customer cleaned in spring is a lead for next spring. A tool that stores the last service date and the rooms cleaned saves you the first five minutes of every call.

Published prices hide real costs in the add-on lists. Service Fusion lists job photo uploads, job costing and customer web portal as add-ons on Starter, without prices. Workiz lists a phone system and marketing campaigns as paid add-ons, also without prices. Ask for a full quote.

Unlimited users on Service Fusion matters for seasonal help. Many carpet companies add helpers in busy months. A per-seat plan charges for each helper, while an unlimited plan does not.

Which tools handle carpet cleaning invoices and the books?

Wave and QuickBooks Online handle invoices and bookkeeping, and most job apps sync to one of them. Carpet cleaners often collect at the door, so payment fees count as much as the plan price.

  • Wave: Starter is $0 and Pro is $19 a month billed monthly. Both allow unlimited estimates and invoices. Card payments on Starter cost 2.9% plus 60 cents. Limit: it has no scheduling, so it pairs with a job app.
  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is listed at $38 a month, with a 50% promotion for the first three months. Essentials is $85 for three users. Limit: Simple Start allows one user.

Keep a clean split between sales and sales tax. Rules vary by state, so ask your accountant how cleaning services are taxed where you work. Whichever tool you pick, set the tax rule once and test it on a sample invoice.

On a $180 whole-house clean paid by card, Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, which is about $5.52 in fees. Wave Starter lists 2.9% plus 60 cents, about $5.82. The gap is small per job and adds up over a busy month.

Deposits are rare in this trade. Large commercial jobs are the exception. Ask each vendor whether it can text a payment link, and whether the customer sees one clear total.

Ask whether the job app syncs paid invoices to your books. Jobber lists QuickBooks Online sync on Connect, and Housecall Pro lists it on Essentials. Without sync, you retype every payment at month end.

What does carpet cleaning software cost for a small company?

A one-van owner can run a working stack for $49 a month, and a growing company lands near $227. These totals add plan fees only, so card fees and taxes come on top.

StackPartsMonthly plan cost
One-van ownerJobber Core billed monthly with no commitment, Wave Starter, Google Business Profile$49
Two-van companyKickserv Start billed monthly, QuickBooks Simple Start at list price$98
Growing companyHousecall Pro Essentials billed monthly, QuickBooks Simple Start at list price$227

Built from the vendor prices above, November 2026. QuickBooks is shown at list price, before its three-month promotion.

Upgrades should follow need, not hope. Move up a plan only when a specific feature, such as routes or reminders, would remove a task you do every day. Moving up because the next plan looks professional only raises the bill.

Annual billing lowers several of these figures, but it ties you to a year. Use the trial first, then prepay. Housecall Pro lists a 14-day trial with no card, and Kickserv lists a 30-day trial.

Seasonality changes the math too. Carpet cleaning often peaks around spring cleaning and the holidays. Ask each vendor whether you can pause or downgrade a plan in slow months, since a month-to-month plan is more flexible than a prepaid year.

Count the cost per job, not per month. A company that cleans 60 homes a month on a $98 stack pays under $2 a job for software. A company that cleans 10 homes a month pays almost $10, so keep that owner on the cheapest tool.

How do carpet cleaners get found before the app matters?

Carpet cleaners get found in Google Maps first. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge, per its own help page.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your carpet cleaning company in Maps and local search with photos, reviews, service area and phone number. Limit: it needs fresh before and after photos and review replies to hold its place.

Before and after photos do double duty. They fill your Google profile and they win quotes, since a homeowner can see a real result. Store them in your job app by customer so you can find them in seconds.

Reviews carry weight in this trade, so learn how to handle a negative review first.

A carpet cleaning site needs pages for room cleaning, pet odor and upholstery, plus a booking form.

How do you choose carpet cleaning software for your company?

Choose carpet cleaning software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it book time windows online, store the rooms cleaned per customer, and text a reminder before the visit?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then divide by your jobs per month.

Setup effort: can you load your price list and customers in a weekend, or does it need a vendor call?

Write down the three tasks that cost you the most time today. Pick the tool that removes those three, not the one with the longest feature list.

A one-van owner should start with Jobber Core, Wave Starter and a free Google Business Profile. That is the whole stack. Add reminders and a second van before you add dispatch.

A multi-van company fits Housecall Pro Essentials or Service Fusion, with QuickBooks for the books. Run the trial on a real week of bookings, since a quiet week hides every scheduling problem.

Review your choice once a year. Prices change, vendors add plans and your own company grows. A tool that fit one van may hold back four, and a yearly check costs an hour.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Ads from carpet cleaning Google Ads and rankings from carpet cleaning SEO bring homeowners in.

What is the best software for a carpet cleaning business?

There is no single best tool, because it depends on van count and how you book. Jobber suits a one-van owner. Kickserv lists 5 users from $60 a month. Housecall Pro and Service Fusion fit larger crews. Test one on a real week of bookings.

How much does carpet cleaning software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Jobber Core is $49 a month with no commitment, and Kickserv Start is $60. Card fees, add-ons and extra seats cost more.

Does carpet cleaning software send appointment reminders?

Several tools do. Kickserv Start lists automated email and text reminders, and Jobber lists automated client reminders on Connect. Reminders cut no-shows and late arrivals, so check that the plan you buy includes them before you commit. Confirm that the text message uses your business name too.

Do carpet cleaners need route or dispatch software?

Only when you run two or more vans. A single van can run on a simple calendar. Housecall Pro lists routes on Essentials, and Kickserv lists dispatch mapping on Run. Pay for them when scheduling becomes the daily bottleneck, not before. Until then a shared calendar does the same job.

Does carpet cleaning software work with QuickBooks?

Several do. Kickserv Start lists QuickBooks Online integration, Jobber adds sync on Connect, and Housecall Pro adds it on Essentials. Confirm that paid invoices sync both ways, so month end takes minutes and not hours of retyping. Ask whether the sync covers customers as well as invoices.

What should a new carpet cleaning company buy first?

Claim a free Google Business Profile, then pick one job app on a free trial. Use Wave Starter at $0 for invoices. Add reminders, a second van and dispatch tools later. Do not buy a full suite before you have steady bookings.

What is the best software for a carpet cleaning business?
There is no single best tool, because it depends on van count and how you book. Jobber suits a one-van owner. Kickserv lists 5 users from $60 a month. Housecall Pro and Service Fusion fit larger crews. Test one on a real week of bookings.

How much does carpet cleaning software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Jobber Core is $49 a month with no commitment, and Kickserv Start is $60. Card fees, add-ons and extra seats cost more.

Does carpet cleaning software send appointment reminders?
Several tools do. Kickserv Start lists automated email and text reminders, and Jobber lists automated client reminders on Connect. Reminders cut no-shows and late arrivals, so check that the plan you buy includes them before you commit. Confirm that the text message uses your business name too.

Do carpet cleaners need route or dispatch software?
Only when you run two or more vans. A single van can run on a simple calendar. Housecall Pro lists routes on Essentials, and Kickserv lists dispatch mapping on Run. Pay for them when scheduling becomes the daily bottleneck, not before. Until then a shared calendar does the same job.

Does carpet cleaning software work with QuickBooks?
Several do. Kickserv Start lists QuickBooks Online integration, Jobber adds sync on Connect, and Housecall Pro adds it on Essentials. Confirm that paid invoices sync both ways, so month end takes minutes and not hours of retyping. Ask whether the sync covers customers as well as invoices.
